prompt: A discrete-mathematics classroom poster demonstrates the one-dimensional cellular automaton 'Rule 30'. There is a horizontal strip of 15 cells. In generation 1 only the CENTER cell (the 8th) is BLACK and all others are WHITE. Each next generation is computed from the one above by Rule 30: a cell becomes BLACK exactly when its left-neighbour, itself, and right-neighbour in the previous row match one of the patterns (left,self,right) = 100, 011, 010, 001 (reading black=1, white=0); otherwise it becomes WHITE. Cells beyond the strip edges count as WHITE. Apply the rule generation by generation and render ONLY generation 8 (the 8th row) as a single horizontal strip of 15 square cells, each cell painted solid BLACK or solid WHITE, in order left to right. Do NOT draw the earlier generations, gridline numbers, or any text.
